rules.title: Xcode build files
rules.explanation: Xcode keeps a copy of every project it builds so the next build is faster. It makes them again the next time you build.

rules.title: Old Xcode app archives
rules.explanation: Finished builds you made to share or publish an app. You can't get these back, so look before removing.

rules.title: Old iPhone debugging files
rules.explanation: Xcode copies these from each iPhone or iPad you connect. It copies them again if you connect that device later.

rules.title: Simulator temporary files
rules.explanation: Files the iPhone simulator keeps to start faster. It makes them again when needed.

rules.title: Downloaded npm packages
rules.explanation: Copies of JavaScript packages npm downloaded before. npm downloads them again when a project needs them.

rules.title: Downloaded Yarn packages
rules.explanation: Copies of JavaScript packages Yarn downloaded before. Yarn downloads them again when a project needs them.

rules.title: Shared pnpm packages
rules.explanation: pnpm keeps one shared copy of every package your projects use. Removing it makes the next install download everything again.

rules.title: Homebrew downloads
rules.explanation: Installers Homebrew already used. Homebrew downloads them again only if it needs to reinstall something.

rules.title: Downloaded Python packages
rules.explanation: Copies of Python packages pip downloaded before. pip downloads them again when needed.

rules.title: Go build files
rules.explanation: Go saves compiled pieces to build faster. It makes them again the next time you build.

rules.title: Downloaded Rust packages
rules.explanation: Copies of Rust packages Cargo downloaded before. Cargo downloads them again when a project needs them.

rules.title: Gradle downloads and build files
rules.explanation: Libraries and build pieces Gradle saved for Android and Java projects. The next build downloads what it needs again, which can take a while.
